subject: Fwd: Sensitive headers & redaction — action plan and discovery items
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medwell.com>
Cc: security@medwell.com
Date: Thu, 09 Nov 2028 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sensitive headers & redaction — action plan and discovery items

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single thread for MedWell's security and engineering teams.

Summary of asks from your side:
- Confirm whether outbound request/response logs that Redwood would store for troubleshooting can contain trace IDs (yes/no).
- Confirm required retention window for audit-friendly logs (30/90/365 days).
- Example of headers you consider "sensitive" (you mentioned X-Correlation-ID and Cookie earlier).
- SOC 2 evidence: can we provide the SOC 2 summary report and the security whitepaper?

What Redwood can provide today:
- Configurable header redaction rules per-tenant (mask, hash, drop). We can apply a hash-only mode so IDs remain linkable without exposing raw values.
- Per-route logging level: request-only / response-only / both, and the option to truncate bodies > N bytes.
- Optional short-lived prefix KV cache masking for user-identifiable tokens to reduce exposure in traces.

Attachments: redaction_spec_v1.pdf (draft mapping of header fields -> mask/hash/drop) and sample_request_response_log_snippet.txt (sanitized example).

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Alex/security: confirm the list of headers you need redacted and required retention window by EOD Friday (2028-11-10).
2) Redwood: provide a short runbook that shows configuration UI + API for rule rollout, plus a one-time sample showing the same log lines with trace IDs hashed.
3) If acceptable, schedule a 30-minute technical handoff with engineering (I can set up Mon/Tue next week).

If there are procurement/procurement docs we should include (e.g., an NDA or DPA reference), drop the link here and I’ll route to our legal.

Thanks — Ava
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medwell.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medwell.com
Date: Thu, 09 Nov 2028 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sensitive headers & redaction — action plan and discovery items

Ava — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below and a couple of clarifying questions.

Answers:
- Trace IDs: we cannot accept raw X-Correlation-ID values in logs. Hashing is acceptable if it is a one-way SHA256 with a per-tenant salt so we can't reverse-map.
- Retention: default is 90 days for application logs; audit copies for escalations must be retained 365 days but we expect them to be exportable on request.
- Sensitive headers: please redact/omit Cookie, Authorization, X-User-Email, X-SSN (if present), and any header starting with X-Internal-. X-Correlation-ID must be hashed as above.

Clarifying questions:
1) Can you confirm whether trace-level sampling can be applied so that full response bodies are only kept for 0.5% of requests? We need a sampling mechanism for cost and privacy.
2) For exported audit logs, can Redwood provide an export with the same redaction rules and a tamper-evident manifest?

We will also want to see the SOC 2 summary and the controls mapping for logging and access. Our security team (security@medwell.com) is cc'd — they may follow up with a short questionnaire.

If you can hash a short snippet of the sample log using the per-tenant salt and include it in the runbook, that would help us confirm the approach quickly.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Director, IT Security | MedWell Health
alex.johnson@medwell.com

Action items (owner in parentheses):

- Document sampling options and whether we support deterministic reservoir sampling at 0.5% or a similar Poisson process; include API flags (Monica).
- Draft a short runbook (1-pager) that shows UI steps to configure header rules and how to export audit logs with manifest (Rachel). Include the SOC 2 summary link if available.
- Legal: I'll follow up separately on DPA/NDA; not blocking our technical demo.

Timeline: if we can have the hashed sample + runbook draft by end of day Monday (2028-11-13), I will forward to MedWell and propose a technical handoff for Tue or Wed.

Notes on implementation constraints: please plan for both mask (redact) and hash modes for headers and for the export path to apply the same rules. For sampling, ensure that when a log is sampled (full body retained), the hashed trace ID still appears so MedWell can correlate with their internal systems.

I'll attach Alex's email below for context when you reply.
